name: math
description: math@1: familiar math-film words (#233), the objects, layout words, animations, rate functions, plots, planes, fields, tables and 3D an agent already knows from the upstream math-film library, each a recipe over the canvas primitives with its conversion stated, expanded at check. A parameter no primitive honors is refused with a fix, never dropped.

Circle.conversion: its parameters by name with the reference's defaults; a unit is the frame's short side ÷ 8 in u (fw, fh), so the frame is 14.22 × 8 units at 16:9; y flips and the origin moves to the frame's center; radians become degrees; a stroke width w becomes w × unit ÷ 100 u; font_size f is an em of f ÷ 96 units

Arrow3D.conversion: 3D units are math@1 units, as meters

Scene.play.conversion: each play a cue of a cue.kind@1 verb for run_time seconds; rate functions are ease@1 entries or pulses

ValueTracker.conversion: a named value, data/<id>, which formulas read and cues key

next_section.conversion: a stage marker at the start of the next play

Create.conversion: Create (once ShowCreation, its older spelling) is the cue verb create: a path build from start to end over run_time, the play's rate function its ease

ShowCreation.conversion: Create (once ShowCreation, its older spelling) is the cue verb create: a path build from start to end over run_time, the play's rate function its ease

Write.conversion: the text's or vector's write_on over run_time

FadeIn.conversion: shift and scale are the verb's, shift in u (unit × the reference's)

FadeOut.conversion: shift and scale are the verb's

DrawBorderThenFill.conversion: the outline builds, then the fill rises

GrowFromCenter.conversion: the scale rises from 0 about the center

Transform.conversion: match_morph by arc length onto target_mobject

ReplacementTransform.conversion: match_morph onto target_mobject, which takes its place

TransformMatchingTex.conversion: match_morph pairing the typeset parts by their ids

TransformMatchingShapes.conversion: match_morph pairing parts by area and centroid

LaggedStart.conversion: lag_ratio × run_time becomes the cue's stagger, lag

Indicate.conversion: scale_factor becomes scale; color becomes role

Circumscribe.conversion: shape Rectangle or Circle becomes rect or circle; buff in u

Flash.conversion: the verb's lines about the point

ShowPassingFlash.conversion: a stretch of the outline passes along it

Wiggle.conversion: scale_value becomes scale, rotation_angle in radians becomes angle in degrees, n_wiggles becomes count

FocusOn.conversion: a spotlight closes on the point

CyclicReplace.conversion: each target takes the next one's place

ChangeDecimalToValue.conversion: the number counts to the value

smooth.conversion: smooth is the logistic sigmoid with k = 10, normalized to run from 0 to 1

rush_into.conversion: rush_into is the first half of smooth, stretched: 2·sigmoid(t/2) with k = 10

rush_from.conversion: rush_from is the second half of smooth, stretched

double_smooth.conversion: double_smooth is smooth on each half

running_start.conversion: running_start is the six-degree Bézier with controls 0, 0, pull, pull, 1, 1, 1, pull −0.5

exponential_decay.conversion: exponential_decay(t) = 1 − e^(−t/0.1), divided by its value at 1 so it ends at 1

there_and_back.conversion: ends at 0, so a pulse: the value goes out by sigmoid(10) and back

there_and_back_with_pause.conversion: ends at 0, so a pulse with a pause of a third of its span

wiggle.conversion: the rate function ends at 0, so a pulse wiggle (count 2); the animation Wiggle is the cue verb wiggle

lingering.conversion: keys at 0 and 0.8 of the span, then hold

squish_rate_func.conversion: squish_rate_func(f, a, b): keys at a and b of the span, eased by f

not_quite_there.conversion: not_quite_there(f, p): the key's value is p of the way, eased by f

add_updater.no_match: an updater runs code every frame, which has no closed form: drive the value with a driver (driver@1, an expression over t and named values), or bake the frames with the bake route
add_updater.conversion: none: an updater is code, never data

always_redraw.no_match: a redraw each frame is code with no closed form: drive what changes with a driver (driver@1), or bake the frames with the bake route
always_redraw.conversion: none: a redraw is code, never data

UpdateFromFunc.no_match: a function run each frame has no closed form: drive it with a driver (driver@1), or bake the frames with the bake route
UpdateFromFunc.conversion: none: an updater is code, never data

math.description: math: the familiar math-film palette by its names on a black ground, white ink, yellow accent and the math face, each palette name a role.
limits: A palette name draws only in this look: in another look, color words fall back to its roles
Flat fills and exact lines: no sheen, gradients only as paint gradients
